newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed creates new company from 10 units.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed creates new company from 10 units.

text.p: Lockheed Martin said on Thursday it will reposition 10 of its business units as an independent company co-owned by Lockheed, Lehman Brothers Capital Partners III LP and a management team of former Lockheed executives.

The $525 million deal is expected to close within 45 days. Lehman will own about 50 percent of the new company, L-3 Communications; Lockheed will retain 35 percent, and the management team will have 15 percent.

The units to be combined are Advanced Recorders in Sarasota, Fla.; Communications Systems in Camden, N.J.; Conic in San Diego; Display Systems in Atlanta; Hycor in Woburn, Mass.; Microcom in Warminster, Pa.; Narda Microwave in Hauppauge, N.Y., and Rancho Cordova, Calif.; Randtron in Menlo Park, Calif.; Telemetry & Instrumentation in San Diego; and Wideband Systems in Salt Lake City.

Headquarted in New York City, L-3 will have 5,000 employees and combined 1996 revenues of more than $650 million. Its chairman and chief executive be Frank Lanza, who was president and chief operating officer of Loral Corp when it combined with Lockheed in 1996. Robert LaPenta will be president and chief financial officer, Lockheed said.
